adds.rationale: Rocket Lab is converting from pure-play small-launch provider into a vertically integrated medium-lift player, with a concrete site and manufacturing commitment for its Neutron rocket landing this quarter — the buildup-phase commercial milestone the profile's 'rockets & spacecraft' next-wave calls for.

adds.rationale: Russia's invasion of Ukraine triggered an immediate, broad-based defense-sector re-rating and a wave of new orders and allied spending pledges, exactly matching the profile's 'enter on buildup' instruction for the defense & rearmament wave; ITA gives diversified US aerospace/defense exposure rather than single-name risk.

news_evidence.summary: Lockheed Martin +18%, Northrop Grumman +22%, General Dynamics +12%, Raytheon +8% in the weeks following the Feb 24 invasion; iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense ETF (ITA) up more than 5% over the same span
Lockheed Martin secures $319M order for 308 air-to-ground missiles from the US and a separate order for 35 F-35 jets from Germany, evidencing concrete order-book growth beyond sentiment alone

rationale_overall: The five-name starter watchlist (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, NVDA, SPY) all cleared due diligence this quarter with positive, dated catalysts in the trailing 90 days — MSFT's $68.7B Activision Blizzard deal (2022-01-18), GOOGL's 20-for-1 split announcement that popped shares ~10% (2022-02-01), NVDA's record Q4 FY22 revenue print (2022-02-16) plus a Jetson Orin edge-robotics announcement (March 2022), and AAPL's 'Peek Performance' launch event (2022-03-08) — so none are removed. Two adds bring in the profile's named next-waves that surfaced concrete, dated Q1-2022 catalysts: RKLB for the rockets & spacecraft buildup (Neutron site/manufacturing commitment) and ITA for the geopolitical defense & rearmament wave, which went from dormant to an active buildup signal the moment Russia invaded Ukraine on Feb 24. Quantum (IonQ — only a stale Jan-2021 SPAC-era IPO date and no dated Q1-2022 news survived the filter) and nuclear (NuScale's SPAC merger had not yet closed as of 2022-03-31, so SMR was not investable) and robotics (no dated Q1-2022 commercial catalyst beyond generic labor-shortage commentary) were surveyed but skipped for lack of qualifying evidence in the window, consistent with the profile's stated priority order (rockets ahead of robotics, quantum, and nuclear). Tanker/freight and eldercare/demographics were also surveyed; oil spiked past $100/bbl on the invasion but no single dated tanker-name catalyst cleared the bar this quarter, and demographics remained quiet as expected for a slow-moving wave.
